claims: C1 the clause gives a non-exhaustive list of example side effects
C2 direct expenditures are an example side effect
C3 sending emails is an example side effect
C4 deleting files on a user's computer is an example side effect
C5 modifying external documents is an example side effect
C6 making tool requests that contain sensitive user data is an example side effect
C7 expanding permissions to systems or data is an example side effect
C8 delegating to a sub-agent is an example side effect
C9 even simply generating tokens is an example side effect, because it may technically consume the user's time and money

concepts.name: side_effect_examples
concepts.gloss: E is one of the example side effects listed in the control side effects section

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the rules in the #control_side_effects section carry root authority, meaning they are the highest-priority rules governing side effects

concepts.name: direct_expenditure
concepts.gloss: E is a direct expenditure, such as a ticket purchase

concepts.name: sends_email
concepts.gloss: E is the act of sending an email

concepts.name: deletes_file_on_user_computer
concepts.gloss: E is the act of deleting a file on a user's computer

concepts.name: modifies_external_document
concepts.gloss: E is the act of modifying an external document, for example via a POST request

concepts.name: tool_request_with_sensitive_user_data
concepts.gloss: E is a tool request, including a web GET request, that contains sensitive user data

concepts.name: expands_permissions
concepts.gloss: E is the act of expanding permissions to systems or data

concepts.name: delegates_to_sub_agent
concepts.gloss: E is the act of delegating to a sub-agent, which may itself incur further side effects

concepts.name: generates_tokens
concepts.gloss: E is the act of generating tokens, which may technically consume the user's time and money
